seal.statement: The two DT6 formation falsifiers (dt6-formation-ledger-quorum-spread-first, dt6-voter-surplus-promotion-drain-livelock) are green on the owner clock. They went red on this branch when RebalanceCoordinator.nowFn and the replica-operation repository stopped reading ambient time (22420f874): both scenarios had passed only because their virtual rows were compared against wall-clock now. Two production defects that the dual clock had hidden are repaired at their owner: (A) the repository's visibility-confirmation and read-retry loops read their deadline from the repository's TimeSource but slept on the platform clock, so under a virtual clock the deadline was never approached - both waits now sleep on the same clock their deadline reads (live: RealTimeSource, byte-identical); (B) the recent-completed-self-move lease on the operation ledger held the ledger's own quorum-spread cure REPLACE - the move the QUORUM_SPREAD hold orders first - re-opening the run-22 gap between the first and second spread moves; the lease now exempts the engaged cure through the same actuals relation that exempts it from the hold, with the source replica's node read from the placement rows the concentration evaluation reads. No timeout or budget is raised, no falsifier is weakened, and the voter drive's visibility confirmation is made clock-honest (a deadline of zero on a clock the drive holds still) rather than riding the platform clock.

text: THE TWO REDS WERE NOT DELIBERATE. Both DT6 falsifiers are GREEN on main (1c9f62017) and at this branch merge-base (0675e87f1) and turned red on this branch; git bisect over the ledger falsifier names 22420f874 (formation-sim: the simulator substrate is deterministic) as the first bad commit - the commit that made RebalanceCoordinator.nowFn a projection of the owner TimeSource and gave the replica-operation repository its own TimeSource threaded from the coordinator. Their owner quests (formation-ledger-quorum-spread-first, formation-voter-surplus-promotion-deferral-livelock, epic legacy) are terminal solved since July; nothing in them was pending. Every earlier note on this branch that called these two inherited deliberate reds (F, AddressManager, calibration, charged host) is corrected by this finding: they were regressions of clock correctness, exposing that both scenarios had passed only because their virtual rows were compared against wall-clock now.

LEDGER FALSIFIER (dt6-formation-ledger-quorum-spread-first): with the owner clock the recent-completed-self-move lease (SOURCE_RECENT_LEDGER_SELF_MOVE_LEASED, PRIORITY_RECENT_INTENT_TTL_MS = 2 min) became live - the first spread completion is now recent - and it threw safety_blocked for the SECOND spread REPLACE (r3 off the seed), which the falsifier rightly treats as fatal: the quorum-spread-first design orders both spread moves before any dependent admits, and a lease that holds the second spread re-opens the run-22 gap. The lease doc says it holds EXACT placement off a settling ledger; it never meant the ledger own cure. Repair at the owner: the lease exempts the engaged quorum-spread cure REPLACE through the same relation that exempts it from the QUORUM_SPREAD hold (isEngagedLedgerQuorumSpreadCureMove: concentrated, spread actionable, source on the hottest node), with the source replica ACTUAL node read from the placement rows the concentration evaluation reads (coordinator.systemTableCache; the repository copy of the cache is empty in the DT6 composition, which is a test wiring fact, not a production one). The existing lease witnesses (spread ledger still leased) stay green; two new cases: cure admitted after a recent self-move, and a REPLACE whose source is NOT on the hottest node stays leased even when the move DECLARES the hot node as its source (actuals decide, c-actuals).

VOTER FALSIFIER (dt6-voter-surplus-promotion-drain-livelock): cycles 0-59 took 45 ms of wall time; the hang began when the virtual 60 s voter-ready timeout fired and the REAL failOperation chain ran. The repository visibility-confirmation loop reads its deadline from the repository TimeSource (virtual, +5 s) but slept on the platform clock (setTimeout 200 ms): under a clock the drive holds still, the deadline is never approached and the loop spins in real time forever (tap timeout at 30 s). The retryable-read loop had the same shape (deadline on timeSource, sleep on the platform). Repair at the owner: both waits sleep on the repository TimeSource (RealTimeSource delegates to the platform, so live is byte-identical). The drive then still cannot await an owner operation inline while a wait on its own clock is pending, and the falsifier had already documented the mixed-clock assumption in its own words (keep the (real) confirmation loop fast: its deadline rides the platform clock, not the virtual clock; timeout 100 / retry 5): that block now sets both to zero with the reason recorded - the confirmation observes once and answers on the clock the drive holds. No assertion was removed; the file passes 40/40 as on main. Witness: replica-operation-repository-owner-clock-waits.test.js drives a VirtualTimeSource and expects both loops to settle on it - red on revert (both cases) with the platform waits.

Owner-clock repairs behind the two DT6 falsifiers: (A) replica-operation repository waits (visibility-confirmation retry, authoritative-read retry) sleep on the repository TimeSource, the clock their deadlines read; (B) the recent-completed-self-move lease exempts the engaged quorum-spread cure REPLACE by the hold own actuals relation, source node read from the placement rows the concentration evaluation reads. Witnesses: test/rebalancer/replica-operation-repository-owner-clock-waits.test.js (new), two cases added to test/rebalancer/recent-completed-replace-target-visibility.test.js, the voter falsifier visibility block made clock-honest (0/0 with the reason in the file). Probe scripts/checks/rebalancer-owner-clock-dt6.js: sealed at metric 3 (W-A, lease file, ledger DT6 red with both repairs reverted), now 0; each repair reverted alone turns its own witness red.

VERIFICATION ROUND 1 (independent verifier, approve with concerns): probe 0; both falsifiers 26/40 assertions on branch and on main; red at HEAD without the repairs reproduced (safety_blocked, timeout); repairs A and B red-on-revert reproduced; production cache identity confirmed (lifecycle passes the same cache to the repository and syncOwnerDependencies re-syncs it, so reading coordinator.systemTableCache in the exemption is the same snapshot the concentration evaluation reads); voter block judged honest (one local + one authority observation, then the deadline; the fixture SQL engine is synchronous so the old 100 ms cushion exercised no lag). MEDIUM concern acted on in this attempt: waitForOperationPersistRetry (replica-operation-repository-mutation-gateway-methods.js) slept on the platform clock while both persist-retry loops measure their budget on the repository TimeSource - the same shape as A, not on either DT6 path. Repaired the same way (repair C) with a third witness case (persist retry settles on the repository clock; red on revert). LOW concerns recorded, not acted on: the REPLACE arm of isEngagedLedgerQuorumSpreadCureMove does not check the target against feasibleTargetNodeIds (inherited from the hold relation and the topology-guard caller); placementRows[0] is order-dependent should a replica ever have two service rows; four other platform timers in src/rebalancer are single-clock loops and outside this quest.

Repair C after verification round 1: the persist-retry wait sleeps on the repository TimeSource, the clock its budget is measured on; witness case 3 in replica-operation-repository-owner-clock-waits.test.js (red on revert). Scope otherwise identical to the previous attempt.

Independent verifier (subagent) round 1 approve with one MEDIUM concern (persist-retry wait on the platform clock), acted on as repair C; delta re-verification approve: gateway hunk is exactly the owner-clock wait, witness 16/16, repair C red-on-revert alone (case 3 red, cases 1-2 green), eslint clean, both persist budgets measured on the repository clock so the wait now matches; live default RealTimeSource byte-identical. Evidence in the verifier reports: probe 0, falsifiers 26/40 on branch and main, red at HEAD without repairs (safety_blocked, timeout), repairs A and B red-on-revert, production cache identity confirmed via lifecycle + syncOwnerDependencies, replica-operation and ledger suites 17/17 (885 assertions), ambient intrinsics 0.

LANDING PROOF (widened, 1926 tests): every unit shard green - the two DT6 falsifiers included - and the serial integration lane red on two files. (1) message-group-multi-join-formation (table-scoped discovery should keep postgres-wire replicas route/schema ready, five nodes) is RED ON MAIN as well (346 s, same assertions): the PG-wire endpoint family recorded since PR #30, pre-existing and outside this quest. (2) managed-split-admission-reliability (degraded publication evidence should settle while the source quorum stays readiness-routable, then the deferred-admission assertions) is GREEN on main, RED at this branch clean head 6b305a2fa WITHOUT the DT6 working-tree changes - a third regression of this branch lineage, under bisect over 0675e87f1..6b305a2fa. The DT6 repairs are not implicated in either.

THIRD REGRESSION OF THIS LINEAGE (scope widened, R16): managed-split-admission-reliability.integration.test.js (degraded publication evidence should settle while the source quorum stays readiness-routable) is green on main, red at 6b305a2fa without the DT6 changes; bisect names 5da0d7348 (remove safety reads the owner surface), the first commit of the branch. Traced layer by layer with probes on both trees: the degraded publication mode IS visible; what never happens is routability under CONTROL_PLANE_RECOVERY_ELIGIBLE, because runtimeAuthority.recoveryEligible needs priorityRecoveryActive (plus transport-backed grace) and the rebuilt readiness snapshot reports priorityRecoveryActive false. The planner candidate (AVAILABLE sync answer) says priority_spread_pending / active on both trees; the merge folds the snapshot own direct publication row, and THAT row differs: on main it is the AVAILABLE best-effort planning answer (spread pending, gate active, unsatisfied); on the branch it is the AUTHORITATIVE owner read (steady_published, gate inactive, priorityPartitionSummary satisfied) because 5da0d7348 rewired membership-publication-coordinator-planning.js candidate derivation from getMembershipPublicationPlanningSnapshotBestEffort to getPriorityRecoveryPlanningAnswerForOwnerRead - the substitution the read-policy module it introduced forbids for planning consumers (AUTHORITATIVE is the REMOVE-safety contract only). Repair D: the coordinator candidate takes the AVAILABLE planning answer again (the surface is synchronous now, so no latency race exists to justify the owner read); the integration witness passes (31 assertions), control-plane 178/178, bootstrap 170/170. A memo-identity change I tried first (keying the CL-034 merge memo on the candidate object) did not fix it and is NOT included; the stale-merge hazard it addressed is real but unwitnessed, recorded here for a follow-up. The second integration red, message-group-multi-join-formation, is red on main too (PG-wire family) and stays outside this quest.

Repair D (scope widened per the third-regression finding): membership-publication-coordinator-planning.js derives the membership candidate from the AVAILABLE planning answer (getMembershipPublicationPlanningSnapshotBestEffort, synchronous now) instead of the owner read; witness test/control-plane/membership-publication-candidate-planning-surface.test.js (candidate holds the AVAILABLE answer by identity, owner read never called, nested derivation untouched; red on revert); the probe now also runs that witness and the managed-split admission integration falsifier. Repairs A-C unchanged.

Independent verifier (subagent) delta D approve: single-commit provenance (5da0d7348) and main coordinator surface confirmed; red at head with the hunk reverted; witness 6/6 and red-on-revert; managed-split falsifier 31/31 alone; probe 0 over six witnesses; control-plane 179/179; eslint and ambient intrinsics clean. Judgment: the coordinator is a planning consumer, the policy module itself forbade the owner-read wiring, and the owner read was mutually recursive with the candidate derivation at branch head. Earlier verdicts for A-C stand; combined staged set approved. Follow-ups named, not landed: the CL-034 merge-memo candidate-identity hazard; the multi-join PG-wire integration red on main.

CORPUS, LAND 3: every shard green except the seven-node convergence probe (message-group-multi-join-formation), which is red on main as well and never runs in CI (its primary class convergence-probe is excluded from test:all; a recorded half-implemented decision, 6fcb63299). Root: meta services ship at replica_count 0 and the runtime lifecycle publishes sys-postgres-wire only after placement (PR #30), so the probe waited 6 x 30 s for replicas that are never desired. Re-expressed as a direct commit in the shape of 3120bb196 (PR #42): discovery must advertise the boot-owned admin-meta service route/schema-ready on every node and no postgres-wire replica before a runtime is placed; 94 assertions green in 97 s. Recorded with eight further testing-time quests in solve/epics/apparatus-release-consolidation.md (Testing time, 2026-09-17). Not part of this quest scope.
